 The Athletic: Quentin Grimes leads Lakers’ OT win, shares moment with mother
 Grimes delivers a career night, leading the Lakers' comeback before giving his game jersey to his Mom.
 Dan Woike, The Athletic
 November 18, 2026 3:12 PM Quentin Grimes scored a career-high 47 points in the Lakers’ overtime win over the Hornets.
 Editor’s Note: Read more NBA coverage from The Athletic  here . The views on this page do not necessarily reflect the views of the NBA or its teams.  
 * * *
 LOS ANGELES – Sometimes, a mother just knows.
 Tonja Stelly watched Quentin Grimes go through pregame warmups Tuesday night and thought he moved a little differently. He was super focused, yet he looked energetic. He was locked in, but at the same time, seemed a little more joyful. It wasn’t the kind of thing she could easily put into words.
 It was more of a feeling. Sometimes, a mother knows.
 After Grimes almost single-handedly ensured that the Los Angeles Lakers would win their ninth straight game, he pointed to the stands near the tunnel and motioned for Stelly to come down to the court. One day after they celebrated Tonja’s 60th birthday at Cocina Alba, Quentin gave her his jersey — the one he wore the night he scored 47 points and made the second-most 3-pointers in team history.
 QUENTIN GRIMES WENT OFF!
 🏀 47 PTS (career-high)
🏀 10 3PM (career-high)
🏀 Game-tying 3 to force OT
🏀 LAL 9th straight W
 He joined Kobe Bryant (12 on Jan. 7, 2003) as the only players in Lakers franchise history to record 10+ 3PM in a single game 🤯
 pic.twitter.com/Qm62ovsJvL 
 — NBA (@NBA) November 18, 2026 
 Grimes hit a game-tying 3, forced a key overtime turnover and sealed the Lakers’ 118-114 win over the Charlotte Hornets, bringing the team back from an 18-point second-half deficit. In the fourth quarter alone, Grimes scored 21 points, including a stretch when he had 15 straight points for the Lakers.
 “It was pretty surreal,” Stelly told The Athletic. “I mean, they all work super hard to have moments like this. But you got to lock in and stay focused, enjoy your few minutes of fame like that, and then it’s on to the next.”
 If this sounds like an experienced sports mom, it’s because Stelly is one of one. She’s the only mother with sons playing in the NBA and NHL at the same time; Grimes’ brother Tyler Myers, is in his 18th NHL season as a defenseman, currently playing for the Dallas Stars. She’s seen her children compete at the highest level.
 And she’s seen Grimes make big shots.
 Still, late Tuesday night, with the game on the line, Tonja and her husband Ken paced up and down their row, which had emptied — partly because the game took nearly three hours after an 8 p.m. Pacific Time tip and partly because the Lakers sure looked like they were headed for a loss no matter what Grimes cooked up.
 Even though Luka Dončić scored 36 points, he looked disjointed for most of the night because of frustration with the referees and his early foul trouble.
 Dončić was called for three fouls in the first quarter, the last coming on an off-hand shove that the Lakers challenged and lost. He was called for his fourth foul right before the end of the first half. The Lakers had to play more zone defense than JJ Redick wanted, with Charlotte getting open look after open look from 3. The Hornets made 18 of them.
 But behind Grimes’ fourth-quarter heater, though, they crawled back into the game. Still, a trio of end-of-regulation errors — a badly missed Dončić 3, an ill-advised Ziaire Williams foul and a Matisse Thybulle turnover on an inbounds pass — threatened to snap their winning streak.
 But the Hornets couldn’t put the Lakers away, turnovers and missed free throws opening the door for Grimes to hit his biggest shot at a Laker.
 With the team down by three, Thybulle corralled a White miss from the line and got the ball to Dončić, who led the Lakers on the break. With four defenders pushing over to keep him from taking his favorite shot on the floor — the stepback 3 from the left wing — Dončić zipped a pass to Grimes, who had a hand in the air calling for the ball.
 “All I had to do is raise up and knock it down,” Grimes said.
 With 1.7 seconds left, it ripped through the net as the crowd went nuts. He knew. The bench knew. Tonja knew.
 Quentin Grimes took his jersey off and gave it to his mom, I’m sobbing pic.twitter.com/kOwGFciBgl 
 — sarah (@slothanova) November 18, 2026 
 For the Lakers (13-2), their ninth straight win was one of the reference points Redick will point to throughout the season.
 “One of the things we set out to be was resilient,” Redick said. “As you go along your journey, there are trials, there are ordeals, and that’s how you build resiliency.”
 Tuesday, the toughness came from the Lakers playing without Walker Kessler for the first time this season; he rested a lower-leg injury on the first night of a back-to-back. Austin Reaves missed his second straight game with a heel bruise. Without Kessler, Kevon Looney and two-way rookie Carson Cooper at center. And with Reaves sidelined and the Lakers needing offensive punch, Collin Sexton and Sandro Mamukelashvili made just four shots in a combined 20 attempts.
 “It’s pretty amazing,” Dončić said. “It just explains what kind of team we have. Every other game, somebody else is going to be a hero, but we’re all in this together. Today Q was amazing. But it’s the whole team. The whole team believed in it, the fans believed in it, so it’s just amazing to be part of it.”
 For Tonja Stelly, it was pretty amazing to witness it again.
 As she waited for Grimes to finish with his postgame treatment and media obligations, she was asked about the first time her son was the hero. As a sixth-grader, Grimes hit a game-winner from the corner with his mom at the scorer’s table keeping the official stats.
 “He shot it and was leaning to the left, and it went in and we won the game,” she said with a smile. “It was pretty awesome.”
 Tuesday? That was pretty awesome, too.
 ***
 Dan Woike covers the Los Angeles Lakers for The Athletic. He’s written about professional basketball in Los Angeles since 2011, first for the Orange County Register and most recently for the Los Angeles Times. His work has been recognized by the Associated Press Sports Editors, the Pro Basketball Writers Association, the Los Angeles Press Club and the California News Publishers Association. He’s originally from Chicago. Follow Dan on Twitter @DanWoikeSports.
